deviations.threading_claim_retracted: An earlier version of this record said reduce_sum runs serially because httpstan does not define STAN_THREADS. That was wrong: httpstan/models.py defines it, and what decides threading is STAN_NUM_THREADS, read once at pool start. For THIS launch the effective thread count was not recorded and is not known. The launcher and trainer did not set STAN_NUM_THREADS (the trainer began deriving it afterwards), so Stan's documented default of one reduce_sum thread would apply, but that is inference, not observation. Two separate ps samples were taken during the run: one showed four chain processes at roughly 200% CPU each, and another listed python processes with 8 and 10 OS threads (ps nlwp). nlwp counts every thread in the process, not only reduce_sum threads, and the second sample was not tied to a specific chain process, so neither sample establishes the reduce_sum thread count. A chain at about 200% CPU is more than one busy thread would give, which is why the count is left unverified. 'One thread per chain' and 'two' are therefore both unproven for the reported 53,001 s D~29 fit; its wall time is what it was on an 8-CPU allocation.
